paper.title_en: SoLID and Future Programs at JLab
paper.abstract_en: The Solenoidal Large Intensity Device (SoLID) is a proposed new detector system for Hall A at Jefferson Lab (JLab) with a unique capability of handling high data rates by combining large acceptance and high luminosities ($10^{37}$ to 10$^{39}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$). SoLID at the QCD intensity frontier is the capstone of the JLab 12-GeV science with exceptional potential to lead nuclear physics research worldwide. The three sciencepillars of SoLID include imaging quarks in three-dimensional momentum space inside the nucleon with semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS), extracting the nucleon mass and scalar profile densities and corresponding radii with threshold $J/\psi$ production, and searching for beyond the Standard Model physics and QCD studies with Parity-Violating DIS (PVDIS) process. Additionally, the SoLID collaboration has developed a competitive program on generalized parton distribution functions (GPDs), especially with the double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS) measurement. SoLID will provide data on all three pillars of its scientific program with unprecedented precision and sensitivity in the valence quark region. In this talk, I discuss these three science pillars together with additionally approved SoLID experiments and run-group experiments. I also present selected future programs at JLab such as the MOLLER experiment, and the proposed physics program with a polarized positron beam.
